lessons.title: ו+י: early spelling and doubled letters
lessons.prerequisites: AHY — י as a vowel letter/consonant; VAV — ו sound roles; PREFIXES-MHV — familiar prefixes.
lessons.vocab:
6 new targets
תמונה — picture
נו — well / come on
המון — a lot
אונייה — ship
תווית — label / tag
תא — cabin / compartment
Purpose: Read consonant/vowel roles of ו/י and the supplied double-letter spellings using only known letters.
lessons.sentences:
1. האונייה מהאי.
2. התמונה והתווית מאמא.
lessons.practice: Retrieve the already-modelled readings of יין and היי. Contrast the sound roles of ו/י in familiar words; explicitly model the spellings of אונייה and תווית. Meaning recognition and recall for all current targets. Read the two sentences and identify origin versus gift-giver. Use label/cabin/picture cues and the phrase המון מים for word/phrase practice; do not label fragments as full sentences. Only two cumulative sentences are supplied at this constrained early stage.
lessons.exercises:
1. Choose the word for a ship.
→ אונייה

2. Choose the word for a label/tag.
→ תווית

3. Read: a lot of water.
→ המון מים
notes:
Source: Components!A6

Current approved teaching scope — spacing revision, 25 October 2026:
An early reading/spelling lesson after the known ו roles and prefixes, before לשז. Retrieve יין and היי with their already-supplied readings; do not claim their two yods arise from one identical rule. Model אונייה and תווית with curated audio and explain the relevant doubled spelling before practice. Other new words use known letters. No full-alphabet prerequisite and no new letter/nikkud system. First-contact notes remain at AHY/NOMINAL. More examples return at their later vocabulary introductions.

Guy approved the sequencing changes. Generated examples remain proposed teaching wording; native audio and curated Nikkud require human authoring.

Rebuilt early reading selection, 25 October 2026. תמונה/נו/המון moved from VOWELS-OU; all six former VAV-YOD-SPELLING entries retained later. Three added target meanings support the readable early stage. אונייה: https://www.pealim.com/he/dict/5606-oniya/ ; תווית label/tag: https://www.milononline.net/התווית ; תא cabin/compartment: https://www.pealim.com/he/dict/6643-ta/ . These are source-checked lexical forms, not human-approved new teaching text. Final audio/Nikkud remain to be authored.
Focus: spelling of אוויר, חוויה, תקווה and עירייה; טיול is the single-י contrast. These are unpointed spelling examples, not a blanket consonant-doubling rule.

lessons.title: demonstratives
lessons.prerequisites: LSHZ — לשז; NOMINAL — nominal statements; gender recognition from known nouns is introduced here.
lessons.vocab:
12 new targets
זה — this, masculine
זאת — this, feminine
אולי — maybe
מילה — word
שם — there
מזל — luck
אימייל — email
וילון — curtain
שמש — sun
שן — tooth
לשון — tongue
ימין — right side
Purpose: Use זה/זאת with known nouns and identify their gender; productive gender pairs follow at NOUN-GENDER.
lessons.sentences:
1. זה אמן.
2. זאת אמא.
3. זה יין.
4. זאת מונית.
5. זה תות וזאת תאנה.
lessons.practice:
1. Meaning + recall: practise all current new targets in D through mixed meaning recognition and recall.
2. Apply: Model this is with זה/זאת and already-readable nouns. Identify masculine/feminine noun gender with persons and objects, without treating all endings as predictable. Productive person pairs wait for NOUN-GENDER after ד.
3. Produce: respond to a changed cue with current and earlier vocabulary. Revisit the needed earlier material in the next lesson.
lessons.exercises:
1. Identify a pictured taxi with this is.
→ זאת מונית.

2. Identify a pictured artist with this is.
→ זה אמן.
notes:
Source: Components!F7

Current teaching scope — revised 24 October 2026:
Identify gender with familiar nouns such as אמן/אמא and יין/מונית; explicitly model זה/זאת. This lesson introduces recognition, not a universal noun-ending rule. NOUN-GENDER later teaches productive person pairs after ד is readable. איזה/איזו move to QUESTIONS-BASIC with פה/איפה. משהו and מישהו are vocabulary at FINDING-SOMEONE before clause embedding at EMBEDDED-CLAUSES.

Spacing revision, 25 October 2026: Retrieve the early ו/י spelling explanation at the first relevant doubled spelling in this vocabulary; give the word-specific audio/pointed model rather than asking learners to infer it.

דלת — door

גן — garden

דלי — bucket
Purpose: Read ב/ג/ד in concrete words, preparing for meaningful gender pairs in NOUN-GENDER.

1. זה אבא.
2. הדג מהים.
3. זאת דלת.
4. הדלי מאמא.
lessons.practice:
1. Meaning + recall: practise all current new targets in D through mixed meaning recognition and recall.
2. Apply: Read ב/ג/ד in בית, אבא, דלת, יד, דג, גן, גל and דלי. Contrast the two ב sounds with native word models. Use familiar זה/זאת and source phrases; יש/אין are later.
3. Produce: respond to a changed cue with current and earlier vocabulary. Revisit the needed earlier material in the next lesson.

→ הוא אבא.

2. Make דלת definite: the door.
→ הדלת

Preserve ב/ג/ד as one letter group. VOWELS-OU and DEMONSTRATIVES-SG intervene after לשז; feminine pairs follow immediately now that ד is readable. Demonstratives may be used; יש/אין have not yet been taught.

lessons.title: feminine
lessons.prerequisites: BGD — readable ד; DEMONSTRATIVES-SG — noun-gender recognition; PRONOUNS/NOMINAL — pronouns and nominal statements.
lessons.vocab:
6 new targets
ילד / ילדה — child, masculine / feminine
תלמיד / תלמידה — student, masculine / feminine
דוד / דודה — uncle / aunt
יהודי / יהודייה — Jewish person, masculine / feminine
איש / אישה — man / woman
בן / בת — son / daughter
Purpose: Connect noun gender to useful people words and familiar pronouns.
lessons.sentences:
1. הוא ילד והיא ילדה.
2. אני תלמידה.
3. היא דודה.
4. היא אישה והוא איש.
5. הוא בן והיא בת.
lessons.practice:
1. Meaning + recall: use all current new targets in D in short mixed audio/picture/meaning choices and prompted recall.
2. Apply: match people to the six pairs, then change the referent in a known nominal statement. Contrast regular endings with the lexical pair בן/בת and the change איש/אישה. Do not teach gender as fully predictable from spelling.
3. Produce: give a new response from a changed cue, using this lesson's words and previously learned vocabulary.
lessons.exercises:
1. Change the pictured child from a boy to a girl: הוא ילד.
→ היא ילדה.

2. Identify a female student using היא.
→ היא תלמידה.
notes:
Source: Components!F5

Current teaching scope — revised 24 October 2026:
Build useful masculine/feminine person pairs on noun-gender recognition from DEMONSTRATIVES-SG. Contrast ילד/ילדה and תלמיד/תלמידה with איש/אישה and בן/בת. Do not teach all noun genders as predictable from endings.

Spacing revision, 25 October 2026: Retrieve the early ו/י spelling explanation at the first relevant doubled spelling in this vocabulary; give the word-specific audio/pointed model rather than asking learners to infer it.

lessons.title: Early present: two form groups and agreement
lessons.prerequisites: NOUN-PLURALS — plural; ADJECTIVE-PREDICATES — gender/number agreement; LSHZ — shin/sin; HET-AYIN-RESH — ע/ר; PRONOUNS — subject pronouns.
lessons.vocab:
6 new targets
בא — come, present participle
שם — put, present participle (שָׂם)
עולה — go up / ascend, present participle
רוצה — want, present participle
חדר — room
דירה — apartment
Purpose: Use four everyday verbs through two present-form groups, anchored to known adjective agreement.
lessons.sentences:
1. אני בא לכיתה.
2. היא שמה מתנה בחדר.
3. הם עולים לגג.
4. אתן רוצות מים או חלב?
5. הילדות באות לדירה.
lessons.practice:
1. Meaning + recall: establish four actions from distinct scenes, then retrieve all current targets in D. Reuse known noun/adjective agreement.
2. Apply: briefly name בינוני (participle), the form used in present predicates. Model בא/באה/באים/באות, then transfer to שָׂם/שָׂמָה/שָׂמִים/שָׂמוֹת. Next model עוֹלֶה/עוֹלָה/עוֹלִים/עוֹלוֹת and transfer to רוֹצֶה/רוֹצָה/רוֹצִים/רוֹצוֹת. Compare sound AND spelling. These are two recurring present-form groups, not two binyanim or the only shapes. Use short rounds; do not ask for sixteen unrelated memorised forms at once.
3. Produce: mix actions with subject cues; change one gender/number feature, then mix them. Compare אני בא / אתה בא / הוא בא. Contrast שָׂם puts with familiar שָׁם there through audio/context. Use שם/רוצה with indefinite nouns; עולה with לגג and בא with known destinations. PREP-SUFFIXES-ME-HIM-HER/QST supply spaced retrieval before commands. Formal patterns and the Green rule return later.
lessons.exercises:
1. Describe the children coming to the classroom.
→ הילדים באים לכיתה.

2. Describe a woman putting a gift in the room.
→ היא שמה מתנה בחדר.

3. Describe two women going up to the roof.
→ הן עולות לגג.

4. Ask one woman whether she wants milk or water.
→ את רוצה חלב או מים?
notes:
Source: Guy’s explicit selection, 24 October 2026; Components!C27.

Approved scope — 25 October 2026:
בא, שם, עולה, רוצה. Anchor gender/number agreement to ADJECTIVE-PREDICATES and familiar subject pronouns. Present forms do not change for first/second/third person within the same gender/number; do not add an am/is/are word.

Compare two groups: בא/באה/באים/באות and שָׂם/שָׂמָה/שָׂמִים/שָׂמוֹת; עוֹלֶה/עוֹלָה/עוֹלִים/עוֹלוֹת and רוֹצֶה/רוֹצָה/רוֹצִים/רוֹצוֹת. Teach one model per group, then its second verb for supported transfer, before mixing groups. The second group changes final ה in plurals; do not describe it as an unchanged written stem plus endings. Its masculine/feminine singular forms look identical without Nikkud but sound different. These are two present-form groups within Pa’al, NOT two binyanim or an exhaustive classification. Hint that later roots/pattern lessons explain recurring shapes; no root analysis or Green-rule derivation here.

Meaning cues precede form comparison. Contrast already-known שָׁם (there) with new שָׂם (puts) through taught shin/sin, context and audio; do not introduce שֵׁם (name) here. Use indefinite objects with שם/רוצה until את at DIRECT-OBJECT-ET; no infinitive construction yet. עולה here means go up; cost remains a separate later meaning at FINAL-HE-VERBS.

Keep the existing brief בינוני (participle) introduction, anchored to familiar agreement. Broader noun/adjective analysis is not required here. NOUN-ADJECTIVE applies בא as coming/next after noun+adjective/definiteness. עולה as immigrant to Israel is explicitly introduced at ADJECTIVES-YOD. Later concrete noun/adjective returns provide the fuller explanation.

Authoring citation pairs: בא–בא; שם–שם; עלה–עולה; רצה–רוצה. Only present forms/meanings above are taught here. Sources: https://www.pealim.com/dict/28-lavo/ ; https://www.pealim.com/dict/45-lasim/ ; https://www.pealim.com/dict/26-laalot/ ; https://www.pealim.com/dict/12-lirtzot/

Spacing unchanged: PREP-SUFFIXES-ME-HIM-HER and QST intervene before COMMANDS-GIVE-SIT-GO imperatives. PAAL/PRESENT-FOUR-FORMS extend regular paradigms, FINAL-HE-VERBS analyses final-ה/י with familiar עולה/רוצה, and HOLLOW-VERBS analyses hollow roots with familiar בא/שם. גר is introduced in HOME-VISIT; HOLLOW-VERBS analyses it alongside בא/שם. נח remains a new meaning there.
No named Green-rule derivation in this early lesson; use its established later scope at PAST-HE-SHE-THEY/PRESENT-FOUR-FORMS.

Approved scope — 25 October 2026:
Explain root through known ילד/ילדה/ילדים and תלמיד/תלמידה/תלמידים, then connect known אמן to one new family word אמנות. Reusing inflections alone is not a full derivational account; PAAL explicitly returns with לומד/תלמיד once study is introduced. At most one unfamiliar family meaning per root in the initial model. The six new targets include instructional words and סיפור, not six unfamiliar lookalike root derivatives. אמון and אמונה are separated into RELATIVE-CLAUSES and GEMATRIA; neither is used to explain the other on first exposure. lessons.vocab:
12 new targets
מקום — place
שאלה — question
תשובה — answer
מחשבה — thought
רגש — emotion
פעולה — action
תהליך — process
קשר — connection
סדר — order
משקל — word pattern
נושא — topic
סימן — sign / symbol
Purpose: Separate root from pattern using verified familiar examples.
lessons.sentences:
1. המקום הזה יפה.
2. יש לי שאלה.
3. התשובה ברורה.
4. המחשבה הזאת טובה.
5. זאת פעולה טובה.
lessons.practice:
Start from the verified core models identified in the Topic note; meaning comes before form comparison. Demonstrate the specific pattern and supplied forms, then check transfer with the second model. Keep the remaining vocabulary as application in known sentence frames.

1. Meaning + recall: use all current new targets in D across short audio/picture/meaning choices and prompted recall; mix their order.
2. Apply (4–6 questions): Separate root from pattern using verified familiar examples; sort a same-root pair and a same-pattern pair; retrieve new abstract nouns in known nominal frames.
3. Produce: one new response/reading from a changed cue; combine current words with earlier vocabulary. Revisit the needed earlier material briefly in the next lesson.
lessons.exercises:
1. Do שֶׁמֶן and שֶׁמֶשׁ share a root or a vowel pattern?
→ A vowel pattern; their roots differ.

2. Say: this is a thought.
→ זאת מחשבה.
notes:
Source: Components!C3; Components!D3

Progression: CLASSROOM-PROBLEM — Return: root versus pattern across nouns and verbs

Verified core / application distinction — 25 October 2026:
Retrieve familiar שֶׁמֶן and שֶׁמֶשׁ for the shared noun-vowel shape with different consonants. Their meanings are already known; the structural comparison is new. Do not claim every D word has that one pattern. Connect this shape comparison to root preservation in ROOTS; later concrete pattern lessons each identify their own core.

lessons.prerequisites: PATTERNS — roots/patterns; PRESENT-BA-SAM-OLE-ROTZE — present agreement; PRONOUNS — subject pronouns.

11 new targets

כתב–כותב — write
קרא–קורא — read
עבד–עובד — work
מחברת — notebook
עט — pen
עיפרון — pencil
דף — sheet / page
שיעור — lesson
מורה — teacher
שמע–שומע — hear
Purpose: Match an actor to a regular present action.
lessons.sentences:
1. אני לומד בכיתה.
2. הוא כותב מילה במחברת.
3. המורה קורא ספר.
4. אבא עובד בבית.
5. אתה לומד פה או עובד בבית?
lessons.practice:
1. Meaning + recall: use all current new targets in D across short audio/picture/meaning choices and prompted recall; mix their order.
2. Apply (4–6 questions): Match an actor to a regular present action; change the subject while retaining the masculine singular form; complete short school/work sentences using new objects. Past–present pairs in D are teacher citation forms; teach present here.
3. Produce: one new response/reading from a changed cue; combine current words with earlier vocabulary. Revisit the needed earlier material briefly in the next lesson.
lessons.exercises:
1. Say: I write in a notebook, for a male speaker.
→ אני כותב במחברת.

2. Change the subject to he: אני לומד.
→ הוא לומד.
notes:
Source: Components!C4

Approved scope — 25 October 2026:
Extend the known present/agreement concept using למד/לומד, כתב/כותב, קרא/קורא and עבד/עובד. Explicitly connect לומד to known תלמיד; identify ל־מ־ד. The early בא/שם and עולה/רוצה are also Pa’al, with different surface groups. Name the actual binyan rather than implying the legacy numeric labels are a verified original numbering system. מזלג — fork
מנגו — mango
תבלין — spice
חוויה — experience
תקווה — hope
ידע–יודע — know
Purpose: Use לכם/לכן, מכם/מכן and שלכם/שלכן with familiar questions and requests.
lessons.sentences:
1. כמה תפוזים יש לכם?
2. יש לכן מזלגות.
3. התבלין שלכם כאן.
4. תנו לנו מנגו, בבקשה.
5. אתם יודעים?
lessons.practice: Meaning recognition and recall for all current targets. Contrast singular and plural recipients after retrieving the earlier stage. Model לכם/לכן, מכם/מכן and שלכם/שלכן explicitly; both plural genders in this lesson. Change the recipient while holding the command addressee fixed, then change the addressee separately.

1. Say to a group of women: you have forks.

2. Say to a masculine/mixed group: your spice is here.
→ התבלין שלכם כאן.

Approved scope — 25 October 2026:
The first passive-function lesson remains GENERIC-THEY-PASSIVE: active plural with an unspecified agent. Now contrast כתב את המכתב→המכתב נכתב and שלח את ההודעה→ההודעה נשלחה. Teach נכתב/נכתבה/נכתבו and נשלח/נשלחה/נשלחו before production, then the supplied participles in a later stage. Not every Nif’al is passive (known נכנס is not), and not every Pa’al has a usable Nif’al counterpart. Preserve original source label סביל מליצי in provenance, but teach context/register per word. Pu’al and Huf’al have separate later lessons. Sources: https://www.pealim.com/dict/958-lehikatev/ ; https://www.pealim.com/dict/2221-lehishaleach/
